description: MINUS is Snowflake's synonym for the EXCEPT set operator, and it de-duplicates: set1 carries (3,'C') TWICE and the result of MINUS is DISTINCT. It is reversible - the other direction gives set2's own rows. ALL applies only to UNION, so MINUS ALL is 'Unsupported feature', live-verified. The reservedness split between the two spellings is the other half: MINUS is a RESERVED word, refused in every identifier position like UNION and INTERSECT, while EXCEPT is UNRESERVED and freely usable as an alias with or without AS, as a table name and as a column name - and must still parse as the set operator immediately after an EXCEPT alias. Reservedness applies to the bare word only, so a QUOTED "minus" is an ordinary identifier that keeps its case. Converted 1:1 from query/MinusSetOperatorTest (now retired).

steps.sql: CREATE TABLE set1 (id INT, value VARCHAR)
CREATE TABLE set2 (id INT, value VARCHAR)
SELECT id, value FROM set1 MINUS SELECT id, value FROM set2 ORDER BY id
CREATE TABLE set1 (id INT, value VARCHAR)
CREATE TABLE set2 (id INT, value VARCHAR)
SELECT id, value FROM set1 MINUS ALL SELECT id, value FROM set2
CREATE TABLE set1 (id INT, value VARCHAR)
CREATE TABLE set2 (id INT, value VARCHAR)
SELECT id, value FROM set2 MINUS SELECT id, value FROM set1 ORDER BY id
CREATE TABLE set1 (id INT, value VARCHAR)
CREATE TABLE set2 (id INT, value VARCHAR)
SELECT id AS minus FROM set1 WHERE id = 1
CREATE TABLE set1 (id INT, value VARCHAR)
CREATE TABLE set2 (id INT, value VARCHAR)
SELECT id AS "minus" FROM set1 WHERE id = 1
CREATE TABLE set1 (id INT, value VARCHAR)
CREATE TABLE set2 (id INT, value VARCHAR)
SELECT id AS except FROM set1 WHERE id = 1
